Practice Leader – Soils, Geochemistry, Toxicology & Risk

About SLR & The Role

What if your next leadership role could combine world-class science, exceptional people, and genuine regional influence?
As Practice Leader for Soils, Geochemistry, Toxicology & Risk
, you'll lead and inspire experts across Asia Pacific.

This team now includes our existing Toxicology & Risk, Geochemistry and the Soils & Erosion Practices with the recent addition of our Geomorphology Practice
. With the recent acquisition of Hydrobiology
also adding further strengths across this group. This has seen the Practice now reach 40+ consultants
which you will be tasked with managing and growing this team further across Asia Pacific. As a newly formed grouping of some of the best in the business this provides a unique and exciting opportunity for the right person to scale up and shape the business, delivering into this high demand sector.

From mentoring future leaders to steering some of the region's most challenging environmental projects, you'll have the platform, resources and reach to make a significant impact, while accelerating your own career in a highly visible and strategic position.

SLR Consulting is an international environmental consultancy with a globally recognised reputation for providing high-quality tailored services. With offices throughout the Asia Pacific, Europe, North, Central and South America and Africa regions, we are one of a very small number of leading international specialist environmental consultants.

With 24 offices
in the Asia Pacific region and 1200 + staff
, SLR is on an exciting growth trajectory
. We are flexible on location for the right person to deliver in this key role across the offices where our teams are already established and delivering exceptional work.

Responsibilities

Reporting to the Business Unit Director – Earth Sciences,
The Practice Leader is responsible for leading people, achieving financial KPIs, growing client relationships and market share, driving technical excellence, and achieving business growth within their Practice Area, and across the wider business. Other responsibilities will include:

Leading the Practice Area with authenticity, purpose and vigour
Driving growth in line with market trends and opportunities, and actively manages resourcing requirements to facilitate growth
Consistently achieving KPIs across the spectrum of financial metrics, responding to stretch targets as necessary
Managing SLR’s commercial risk through rigorous and informed review of project work and proposals, ensuring adequate backlog and maintaining standards of excellence
Using your proven leadership skills to maintain and grow a high performing practice
Leading by example by working effectively across the Company, fostering collaboration across practices, promoting knowledge sharing regionally and globally
Ensuring the portfolio of projects with the Practice Area is healthy, with a net positive position, and that high risks are appropriately managed
Maintaining a client focus always. Engaging frequently with clients in collaboration with other business leaders to drive brand awareness, business development, and market share advancement both regionally and globally.
Keeping up to date with specialist area trends and best practice, participating in technical and/or professional associations
Living and breathing the SLR way through the promotion and use of consistent globally aligned systems, practices and processes

Experience

Our ideal candidate will have 12-15+ years’ experience, including
experience within a consultancy group
, as well as:

Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Science/Engineering or similar with relevant experience in one or more of soils, erosion, geochemistry, risk assessment, toxicology/eco-toxicology or geomorphology. Post Grad qualifications will be held in high regard.
Experience managing both projects, and teams of consultants across different geographies
Proven experience in operations leadership within a technical consulting or professional services environment
Experience in developing practice-level business plans and achieving intended outcomes, particularly for developing teams in start-up or scale up phases.
Proven people management experience across a wide area to engage, develop and retain their team
Demonstrated experience in consistently achieving performance metrics and growing teams, revenue and margins
Excellent business development, client management and multi-disciplinary bid execution skills
Outstanding ability to understand client needs and oversee teams to meet those needs
Effective communication capabilities, particularly around conveying vision, strategic intent and ability to invigorate people to bring them on the journey
Competence in analytical assessments and reporting
The ability to travel interstate and international to engage with the team personally.

Our Benefits

We are most proud of our expert teams and unique culture and our where we work together to collaborate on projects to get the best possible outcome for our clients.

Whether you’re enjoying our flexible hybrid work environment, taking advantage of our novated leasing offers, or at a time in your life where a supportive and generous parental leave scheme is key, our benefits aim to ensure that we cater for all.

You can find a comprehensive list here.

jobs.description:
Job Description

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower all of our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.

Our pledge to you

Join GHD

That’s the #PowerOfCommittment

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Are you ready to lead a dynamic team of Emergency Response/Preparedness and environmental professionals in tackling some of the most pressing challenges facing our environment today?

Who are we looking for?

As a Project Manager
at GHD, you will not only mentor and guide the team but also take the reins in environmental emergencies, collaborating closely with clients and agencies to ensure effective response and resolution.

Your role will extend beyond project management to include business development and client expansion activities, where your expertise in environmental engineering, geology, or related fields will shine. With 5+ years of project management experience under your belt, including a proven track record in emergency response, client relationship management, and business development, you'll bring a wealth of knowledge to the table.

From conducting environmental sampling and monitoring to spearheading regional visibility initiatives, your passion for environmental stewardship and problem-solving will drive our success. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, possess exceptional communication skills, and are committed to making a difference, join us in shaping a sustainable future. Apply today and Join our Emergency Management (GHD FIRST) team.

This opportunity can be based out of the Chicago office.

Who is GHD FIRST:

GHD Fast Incident Response Services Team (GHD FIRST) delivers turnkey, 24/7/365 incident response and management services throughout North America. The GHD FIRST team provides the following core services:

Emergency Preparedness, Planning, and Drills
Environmental/ Remediation Services
Incident Management / Incident Command System (ICS)
Air Monitoring/ Industrial Hygiene
Waste Management
Toxicology/ Risk Assessment
Geographic Information Systems (GIS)/ Database
Shoreline Clean-up Assessment Technique (SCAT)
Digital Technology/ Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Services
Construction/ Construction Management Services
Crisis Communication and Community Engagement
Litigation Support

GHD has more than 100 offices across North America with over 500 staff trained in emergency response and emergency management procedures. Listed below is a management role currently open to grow and further develop the GHD FIRST business sector within GHD.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Accountable for one or more medium-sized projects of low to moderate complexity with a small- to medium-sized team. Focus on the creation of the project vision and planning documents and manage the implementation, reporting, and performance of the overall project with the expectation of delivering on time, within budget, and to scope.

Document Preparation: Prepare moderately complex documents using a variety of applications for technology devices, such as standard office software. Also responsible for gathering and summarizing data for reports.
Stakeholder Management: Plan and deliver stakeholder engagement activities to develop effective working relationships for projects and to ensure that stakeholder needs and concerns are identified and met.
Personal Capability Building: Develop own capabilities by participating in assessment and development planning activities as well as formal and informal training and coaching; gain or maintain external professional accreditation, where relevant, to improve performance and fulfill personal potential. Maintain an understanding of relevant technology, external regulation, and industry best practices through ongoing education, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.
Continuous Improvement: Contribute to reviewing existing operations in own area of work, and generate new ideas to assist in identifying continuous improvements.
Work Scheduling and Allocation: Assign short-term work schedules to a team of subordinates in order to achieve expectations while following established timelines.
Project Assurance: Conduct assurance reviews within the project, facilitate the delivery of assurance reviews by independent third parties, and take appropriate action to resolve any issues identified, so that senior stakeholders have confidence that the project can deliver according to time, budget, and quality.
Project Scope Definition: Manage the delivery of research, workshops, and other activities to support the specification and agreement of project deliverables.
Project Planning: Produce workstream or project plans, ensuring that all activities are identified, are appropriately organized to deliver project objectives, and comply with the organization's project management framework.
Project Reporting and Review: Draft project review reports and presentations, including key information, commentary, and recommendations, to support the review process and enable stakeholders to evaluate progress and agree on change.
Project Resource Management: Manage the deployment of project resources, proactively managing project costs, providing forecasts, and presenting variances with narrative at appropriate review points to ensure effective utilization.
Project Risk and Issue Management: Identify and evaluate risks, issues, dependencies, and constraints associated with the project, escalating matters where appropriate. Where necessary, develop, agree on, and implement solutions to overcome these concerns.
Project Closeout and Handover: Draft elements of product documentation and user training to support handover to business as usual. Contribute to post-project reviews and identification of lessons learned.
Project Team Management: Lead a small project team; communicate the necessary outcomes and the direction required to achieve them; coordinate team actions on project tasks; request additional team member support when needed; and identify areas of improvement to build the capability of the team through training, coaching, and mentoring.
Requirements Management: Coordinate the identification and elicitation of requirements; conduct analysis of those requirements for completion and alignment; document and manage requirements throughout the life of the project; and coordinate the verification of the end deliverable. Generally done at the level of project phases.
Willingness to respond to call outs during non-routine working hours
Act as the first point of contact for clients for new emergency projects, with ability to delegate tasks and request support as required from GHD FIRST team.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science or a related field

Experience

General Experience: Experience enables job holder to deal with the majority of situations and to advise others (Over 3 years to 6 years)
Managerial Experience: Experience of general supervision of more junior colleagues (7 to 12 months)
Experienced in emergency preparedness, air monitoring, environmental assessment/sampling, ICS, SCAT, PHMSA
Experience with railroad and pipeline related emergencies a plus

Paid time off – Our PTO benefit is designed to provide eligible employees with a period of rest and relaxation, sick, and personal time throughout the year. PTO starts at 16 days per year and increases with years of service

Job Description And Duties

The mission of the Chemical Analysis and Emissions Research Branch is to timely provide accurate measurements of mobile source emissions and fuels and technical expertise to support the California Air Resources Board motor vehicle and clean fuels programs.

The Fuel Analysis and Methods Evaluation Section (FAMES) is looking for an individual with strong work ethics, strong background in analytical chemistry, and good communication skills. The section analyzes motor vehicle fuels at the Southern California Head Quarters (SCHQ) in Riverside. The results are used in determining compliance with the cleaner burning gasoline and clean diesel regulations. FAMES also provides support to the Motor Vehicle Program by analyzing fuels used in emissions testing and providing expertise on the impact of fuel properties on emissions. Both functions require the evaluation, development, and implementation of more precise and accurate methods of analysis. FAMES is also responsible for proposing the adoption of new and updated methods into California regulations.

Under the supervision of an Air Resources Supervisor I, the successful candidate will carry out analyses of motor vehicle fuels using gas chromatography with flame ionization detector, supercritical fluid chromatograph, sulfur analyzer, x-ray fluorescence spectrometry, vapor pressure analyzer, and distillation analyzer. These analyses may be carried out at the SCHQ to prepare technical reports and scientific papers for presentation and publication and perform other duties as required. The candidate will also develop new test methods for the regulated fuel properties. Other duties include completing data and quality control reports, performing routine maintenance on the instruments, procuring supplies, managing service contracts, and developing new analytical methods or improving existing methods. An incumbent may also prepare and edit technical reports and scientific papers for publication and oversee the inventory and disposal of chemical reagents.

jobs.description:
Description

ICF’s Fish and Aquatic Science and Technology Team is in an exciting period of expansion and invites applications for a Senior Data Scientist position. The Senior Data Scientist will work closely with fish biologists, hydrologists, and project managers to assist water resource clients with quantitative analysis, decision support modeling, and publication of applied science. Most immediate assignments will focus on statistical and decision support modeling and publishing work on Chinook Salmon in California’s Central Valley, though there will be opportunities for future work in other regions. Generally, the Senior Data Scientist will manage data and conduct scientific analysis, develop and maintain models and data pipelines, and contribute to proposal writing, study planning, fieldwork, and final deliverables, including report and manuscript preparation.

This position is available in San Francisco, CA, with the flexibility to work remotely.

The Successful Applicant Will Demonstrate The Following

Fish Data Expertise with knowledge of and experience with key issues confronting fish management in Northern California, including Chinook Salmon population dynamics, endangered species recovery, habitat restoration, flow management, and monitoring program design.
Water Management Expertise with knowledge of and experience with key issues confronting water management in California, including reservoir and conveyance operations, water supply and allocation, environmental flows, and drought and flood management. Ability to understand and interpret water operations, hydrologic and hydraulic information, and their implications for fish populations, habitat, and management decisions. Familiarity with California water policy and the legislative process.
Quantitative and Problem-Solving Expertise: Knowledge and aptitude for quantitative analysis to evaluate the effects of clients’ proposed actions; ability to design and apply sophisticated, robust, and creative analytical approaches, including hierarchical and Bayesian statistical models and machine learning; ability to interpret hydrologic, hydraulic, and telemetry modeling outputs and integrate them into fish population and decision-support models; ability to conduct and interpret advanced statistical analyses; and proficiency in R, Python, and SQL.
Open and Reproducible Data Science: Demonstrated ability to design and implement transparent, reproducible, and collaborative scientific workflows consistent with U.S. federal Open Science and Open Data expectations. Experience developing documented, version-controlled analytical workflows; maintaining clear data provenance; automating data processing, analysis, and reporting; and producing reusable data, code, and analytical products. Ability to establish shared workflows and documentation that facilitate collaboration, scientific review, knowledge transfer, and reuse across interdisciplinary teams and agency partners.
Excellent Verbal and Written Communication Skills: Peer-reviewed scientific publication record and experience presenting at professional conferences. Strong ability to accurately and effectively translate scientific findings to inform policy recommendations in workshops and structured decision-making processes.
Ability to express results of analyses to technical and non-technical audiences, including multi-agency stakeholder groups, through technical reports, presentations, and interactive data visualization tools (e.g., R Shiny applications), sometimes in stressful and contentious settings.
Project Management Skills: Ability to manage several simultaneous long-term projects, including budget tracking, staff coordination, client relationship management, and completion of all required products/reports.
Team Leadership Skills: Demonstrated track record of setting high personal performance and quality standards and enabling the team to be successful; viewing all team members as critical and treating team members with respect and professionalism; collaborating and leveraging team member strengths; and mentoring/developing junior team members, including through code review and documentation practices.
Science-Business Balance: Expertise and passion for science, natural resources, and resolving complex fish problems while balancing the need for business acumen, marketing, and expansion opportunities.

Specific Job Duties Will Include

Conducting analyses and leading or assisting with writing scientific documents, technical reports, and peer-reviewed manuscripts for fish-related projects
Developing, updating, and documenting statistical, population, and decision support models for fish and water resource management (e.g., Chinook Salmon recovery and flow decisions)
Building and maintaining reproducible codebases and automated data pipelines that connect monitoring data to models
Meeting with water resource clients to discuss technical aspects of planning, implementation, and monitoring of fish and water resource management projects
Describing projects and interpretation of analyses through written and oral communication and interactive visualizations to a broad audience, sometimes in contentious environments
Conducting scientific research leading to develop of knowledge to inform resource management.
Working with a team of technical staff from multiple disciplines to complete analyses and documentation on time and within budget
Developing scope and budget and writing proposals
Building and maintaining client relationships
Mentoring junior biologists

Education/Minimum Qualifications

Master’s degree in fisheries biology, fisheries and wildlife, quantitative ecology, or equivalent science-related field or
5 years of increasingly complex assignments in fish data science

Additional Desired Qualifications

Ability to demonstrate expert-level integration of complex data sets to facilitate analyses
Demonstrated expertise in quantitative fish science field
Experience conducting scientific research using fisheries expertise
Peer-reviewed publication record in quantitative fisheries science
Experience applying hierarchical or Bayesian modeling tools (e.g., Stan, Template Model Builder) to fisheries data
Experience supporting structured decision making for California water and fish management

jobs.description:
About Exponent

Exponent
 is the only premium engineering and scientific consulting firm with the depth and breadth of expertise to solve our clients’ most profoundly unique, unprecedented, and urgent challenges.  

We are committed to engaging multidisciplinary teams of science, engineering, and regulatory experts to empower our clients with solutions that create a safer, healthier, more sustainable world. If you’ve been thinking about swapping the pace of a major city for a regional lifestyle without stepping back from your career, Bundaberg offers the opportunity to do both.

.

You may already be an established senior professional, or you may be ready to broaden your influence, take on greater client and commercial responsibility and continue developing towards future leadership opportunities.

jobs.description:
Description

Environmental Chemist

Put your analytical skills toward making a positive impact on the planet and your career! Join ICF in support of the US Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) contract at the new Region 9 Laboratory in Corvallis, Oregon.

ICF is looking for an Environmental Laboratory Chemist in support of the USEPA Region 9 Environmental Services Assistance Team (ESAT) contract. ESAT provides analytical, quality assurance (QA), and technical support to USEPA programs such as Superfund and other programs requiring the identification, assessment, remediation, and regulation of environmental hazards. The team performs analysis on soil, water, air, waste, and tissue samples for chemical contaminants using USEPA-approved methods supporting EPA’s mission to protect human health and the environment through programs such as the Drinking Water programs, Clean Water Act (CWA), Clean Air Act (CAA), Superfund (CERCLA).

The Environmental Chemist
will apply their knowledge and work experience to primarily support the preparation and analysis of organic chemistry methods with possible cross-training on various inorganic analyses. All team activities must comply with EPA methods for various media (air, water, soil, biota) and environmental programs as well as the NELAC standard (2016). Job duties include sample preparation in support of and operation of GC-ECD, GC-FID, and GCMS to determine volatile and semivolatile organic compounds, pesticides, Aroclors, and fuel hydrocarbon as well as new and emerging contaminants. The successful candidate must be able to work both independently and as member of a team.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, environmental science, environmental engineering, or related.
Minimum 2 years of laboratory experience using EPA-approved methodologies and instrumentation, preferably GC-FID, GC-ECD and GC/MS.
Excellent verbal, interpersonal and written communication skills, and the ability to think critically.
U.S. citizenship required per federal contract.
MUST BE ABLE TO PASS an EPA background check to obtain access to US federal property.

Preferred Qualifications

Solvent extraction experience using EPA methodologies and CLLE, SPE, ASE and other techniques.
Prior progressive experience in laboratories accredited for environmental analyses (e.g., TNI or NELAC, state programs).
Experience working at Federal facilities.
Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) experience, knowledge of Promium Element LIMS is a plus.

jobs.title: Hazardous Materials Specialist (CUPA)
jobs.description:
PLEASE READ THIS JOB ANNOUCEMENT IN ITS ENTIRETY. An Alameda County Job Application is required to be considered for ALL County recruitments.

Alameda County, Environmental Health Department,
is recruiting for a provisional appointment: HAZARDOUS MATERIALS SPECIALIST

Join our dynamic motivated and compassionate team.

$114,129.60-$136,697.60 Annually

Plus, an excellent benefits package!

This is a provisional recruitment.

*Provisional Appointments:
For a provisional appointment, a civil service exam is not required. However, to obtain a regular position, the appointee will need to compete successfully in a County Exam when open.

ABOUT US

Alameda County
Department of Environmental Health Environmental Health programs impact the lives of Alameda County citizens every hour of each day. Our work protects and enhances the health and quality of life by ensuring food and recreational safety, reducing exposures to toxins and pests, protecting the quality of our water, air, the physical environment and so much more. In many other ways, we work to make your community better as our goal is always environmental health protection.

Learn more about us!

https://deh.acgov.org/index.page

The POSITION

Under general direction, conducts hazardous waste investigations and evaluates and interprets problems of environmental and public health hazards. This position works under the general direction of a Supervising Hazardous Materials Specialist.

DISTINGUISHING FEATURES

The Hazardous Materials Specialists are located in the Certified Unified Program Agency (CUPA), Local Oversight Program (LOP), and the Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) Program, of the Environmental Health Department. Incumbents conduct investigations and site data analysis for industrial, governmental and community sites regarding possible health hazards, environmental impact, or regulatory compliance concerns. The Hazardous Materials Specialist is distinguished from the Environmental Health Specialist in that the latter is primarily responsible for environmental and public health impacts associated with the improper use or storage of hazardous materials or has responsibility for the safe operation of Household Hazardous Waste Facilities, HHWF's. The handling and managing of hazardous waste require a comprehensive knowledge of the hazardous materials field. Incumbents receive directions from a Supervising Hazardous Materials Specialist.

EXAMPLE OF DUTIES

NOTE: The following are the duties performed by employees in this classification. However, employees may perform other related duties at an equivalent level. Each individual in the classification does not necessarily perform all duties listed.

1. Makes recommendations for the elimination, minimization, or control of hazardous conditions; evaluates hazardous waste at the phase of generation, transportation and disposal.

2. Interprets industrial health standards; provides information to the public; prepares correspondence; reports on investigations and evaluations. Provides educational outreach to schools, professional organizations, and other members of the public.

3. Represents the Hazardous Materials/Waste Program in collaboration with industrial hygiene engineers, physicians, safety engineers and representatives of private industry, public utilities and other governmental agencies; provides technical consultation and formal training to management, labor organizations, governmental agencies and civic groups regarding complex hazardous material problems and issues.

4. Gathers supportive data and may prepare documents for the District Attorney’s Office or other administrative agencies to initiate possible prosecution of violations of applicable hazardous materials codes

5. Operates computer systems for data entry and retrieval.

When assigned to the CUPA Program:

6. Conducts routine environmental surveys; investigates potential community health hazards; evaluates work sites; ensures compliance with applicable laws and regulations and local ordinances.

7. Responds to emergency hazardous materials incidents within the County’s jurisdiction; documents, identifies, assesses risk and advises on clean up.

HAZARDOUS MATERIALS SPECIALIST

jobs.description:
Company Description

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Job Description

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your technical and professional excellence and advance your career in a collaborative, inclusive, diverse, and empowering culture? Ramboll is a leading scientific and environmental consulting firm providing a broad range of technical services to both public and private sector clients. When you join Ramboll, you will become part of a company that strives to make a difference – for our employees, clients, and society.

Ramboll is seeking an entry-level consultant to join the Risk Assessment and Community Health group in the firm’s Oakland, CA office. Hybrid work arrangements are available, with office presence required at least two days a week.

Your new role

As an entry-level health sciences consultant at Ramboll, you will support a range of human health risk assessment and community health projects in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. Your work will include independent, detail-oriented technical tasks as well as coordination with colleagues and project teams. Projects may be related to hazardous waste and other contaminated sites, Brownfield redevelopment, vapor intrusion, ambient and indoor air quality, product safety, regulatory interactions, community engagement, and litigation. Tasks may include data management, statistical analysis, fate and transport modeling, spatial analysis, sampling/remediation/risk management planning, and technical reporting. This is a unique opportunity to work with Ramboll experts to advance your technical and consulting skills.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Compiling, organizing, and managing environmental data and databases; performing statistical and geospatial analyses of environmental and health data.
Evaluating the environmental fate and transport of chemicals
Estimating human exposures to chemicals in different environmental media (e.g., air, soil, sediment, fish tissue, produce, water, etc.) and exposure scenarios, and calculating associated health risks.
Assisting with preparation of technical reports, written communication, proposals, and presentations
Reviewing and evaluating technical documents (e.g., scientific articles, regulations)

Qualifications

About you

From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your professional development and advancement in the company! Successful candidates will typically possess:

Advanced degree (M.S., MPH or equivalent) in Environmental Science or Engineering, Environmental Health Science and/or Environmental Toxicology
Exemplary individuals with bachelor’s degree and 2 + years of relevant experience may be considered.
Strong analytical, quantitative, organizational, problem-solving, critical thinking skills, and time management skills; excellent written and oral communication skills
2+ years of chemistry coursework required.
Current authorization to work in the United States on a full-time basis, where required for the position.

Preferred Skills and Experience:

Knowledge of risk assessment, exposure assessment, and fate and transport of chemicals in the environment
Proficiency with MS Office; experience with MS Access or other relational databases (e.g., SQL) for managing, querying, and analyzing environmental data.
Demonstrated strong quantitative and problem-solving skills; experienced with statistical and data analysis using R, Python, SQL, or SAS
GIS capability is a plus.
Experience reviewing and evaluating technical documents, scientific articles, regulations, and regulatory guidance.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Meaningful, high-impact work
Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
Competitive compensation and benefits
Professional development and leadership opportunities
A collaborative and inclusive culture
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $79,040–$98,800 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in the Americas

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Where People Flourish

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. Ready to join us?

PhD in Toxicology or a related scientific field
Minimum of 8 years of consulting experience in the toxicology space

Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex ideas clearly and persuasively to diverse audiences

Adept people management abilities coupled with extensive experience in successfully overseeing and executing complex projects
Strong commitment to professional development

### **Job Description and Duties**

The Fish Restoration Program (FRP) is seeking two creative, curious, and collaborative scientists to help drive cutting edge ecological analysis, interagency coordination, and field based discovery related to tidal wetland restoration across the upper San Francisco Estuary. If you’re excited by the intersection of advanced analytics, restoration science, mentorship, and hands on fieldwork, this is your opportunity to make a direct impact on the future of California’s wetlands.

What You’ll Do

• Lead advanced ecological analyses to evaluate restoration effectiveness and guide adaptive management.

• Synthesize literature, data, and multi program findings into high quality technical reports and peer-reviewed articles.

• Mentor colleagues in data analysis, visualization, and effective scientific communication.

• Work closely with partner agencies to integrate monitoring and synthesis efforts and support responsible data access and use.

• Get outside—conduct boat-based sampling of wetland invertebrates and fishes in and around the eleven FRP restoration projects.

• Support lab operations by sorting invertebrate samples, preparing nutrient samples, and calibrating water quality instruments.

Who You Are

You’re a scientist who enjoys the entire process of transforming samples into knowledge – getting muddy, wrangling data, and communicating findings, while teaching others along the way. You thrive in collaborative, interdisciplinary environments and believe science should be transparent, rigorous, and accessible.

Why This Role Matters

FRP’s monitoring and synthesis will shape California’s wetland restoration planning and management for years to come. Your work will help determine what’s working, why it’s working, and how restoration can be improved to support fish and wildlife in a changing estuary.

Ready to put your analytical, ecological, and communication talents to work for one of the state’s most impactful restoration programs?

Apply today and help build a healthier estuary for future generations.

jobs.description:
**Senior Environmental Scientist**

**Perth, WA | Permanent, Full-time / Part-time**

RPS, a Tetra Tech company, is a leading global professional services consultancy delivering solutions across the environment, infrastructure, energy and urban development sectors.

In Australia Asia Pacific, we work with industry, government and communities to define, design and manage complex projects that create shared value. Our people combine technical expertise with practical thinking to help clients understand environmental risks, navigate complex challenges and deliver successful project outcomes.

As part of Tetra Tech, we are connected to a global network of approximately 30,000 employees, providing access to specialist expertise, opportunities and projects across Australia and internationally.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking a Senior Scientist to join our Oceans & Environment team in Perth, or Margaret River. RPS understand the importance of flexible working arrangements and this role is open to both full-time and part-time hours.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early to mid career environmental scientist who has experience in environmental approvals and is looking to continue developing their technical and consulting capability. Working alongside experienced environmental professionals, you will contribute to a range of projects.

**What you'll be involved in**

Your responsibilities will include:

* Preparing environmental approval documentation under the EP Act and EPBC Act.
* Preparing practical environmental management plans and strategies.
* Prepare and provide environmental advice to clients.
* Manage multiple tasks on a range of projects and effectively deal with conflicting priorities and work to tight deadlines.
* Prepare and provide environmental advice to clients.
* Work as part of a multi-disciplinary team and work co-operatively with people at all levels to achieve outcomes.
* Communicate and maintain good relationships with internal stakeholders, clients, suppliers and project stakeholders.

**About you**

We are looking for someone who is technically curious, practical and keen to build a career in environmental approvals and environmental consulting.

**You will ideally bring:**

* A relevant tertiary qualification in environmental management or environmental science.
* Experience in undertaking environmental impact assessments in Western Australia.
* Understanding of State and Commonwealth environmental legislation, policy and guidance.
* Good technical report writing skills and attention to detail
* Minimum of five years relevant work experience.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* The ability to work independently while knowing when to seek technical guidance
* An understanding of project delivery including quality, safety, time and budget considerations
* A commitment to ongoing professional and technical development

**Why RPS?**

Joining RPS means becoming part of a collaborative environmental team while also having access to the technical capability and opportunities of the broader Tetra Tech network.

You will have the opportunity to develop your career alongside experienced contaminated land specialists, gain exposure to a diverse range of projects and progressively take on greater technical, project and client responsibilities.

**We also offer:**

* Flexible and hybrid working arrangements where appropriate
* Professional development and career progression opportunities
* Paid professional memberships
* Active lifestyle and wellbeing initiatives
* Employee assistance and wellbeing support
* Opportunities to work with technical specialists across Australia and the wider Tetra Tech network
* A supportive and collaborative team environment
* Paid parental leave and other employee benefits

**Our commitment**

RPS is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people are respected, supported and encouraged to bring their individual perspectives and experience to work.

If you have a foundation in environmental science or contaminated land and are looking for an opportunity to deepen your technical expertise while working alongside experienced specialists, we'd like to hear from you.

**Our Approach**

Our people live our purpose, deliver our promise, and demonstrate our behaviours every day. Our behaviours define who we are. Developed by our people, they underpin everything that we do. They create the memorable experiences we are known for and make RPS a great place to do great work.  
Stronger together is one of our five core behaviours and it is key to building a collaborative workplace. We encourage everyone to bring their best and to support others to do the same. By sharing knowledge, challenging each other to think differently, and fostering an environment of trust and respect, our people can learn, grow and thrive – and share in our success.

**Recruitment Agencies**

We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on this list. Please refer to the careers page on our website if you require any further information.

Under the State of California’s new cross-connection control regulations, the SFPUC must review all service connections (~180,000+) to properties in San Francisco, as well as the eight other water systems under SFPUC’s control, to evaluate potential hazards to the public drinking water distribution system arising from activities on user premises. jobs.description:
Toeroek Associates is a dynamic small business provider of specialty consulting and analysis services to the U.S. Government. Our multi-disciplined environmental staff includes scientific, legal, and engineering experts who support federal and state government entities in compliance, remediation, field services, site assessments, oversight, historical and technical research, litigation, and community engagement. Toeroek offers a collaborative and congenial work environment with a team of passionate staff dedicated to finding solutions to complex problems in the fields of environment, records and knowledge management, and national security.

Toeroek Associates is seeking a junior-level Environmental Analyst to provide support in the Denver, Colorado, Sacramento, California, Dallas, Texas, or Chicago, Illinois areas.

**Summary**

The analyst will work as part of a team to assist EPA and other government agencies with administering environmental regulatory compliance and enforcement programs. Our focus is on cleaning up our communities. The analyst will work on multiple contracts, researching and compiling evidence to characterize contamination and identify potentially responsible parties (PRPs) at hazardous waste sites. Superior research, writing, and analytical skills are essential to this position, as is an interest in helping government agencies enforce their environmental regulations.

**Duties include:**

* Assist in identifying sources of information about PRP operations, including federal, state and local agencies, public libraries, private archives, and map and aerial photography archives
* Conduct research to obtain documents pertinent to PRP historical operations and waste disposal practices, as well as environmental regulatory compliance
* Review information on PRP operations, including responses to EPA information requests, facility inspection reports, sampling and investigation reports, hazardous materials inventories and other documents collected, and identify relevant data for purposes of analyzing Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) liability
* Draft evidence summary reports that present information about PRP operations, chemical usage, disposal practices, and soil and groundwater sampling data
* Review laboratory sampling data results for purposes of extracting and summarizing relevant data from sampling and investigation reports
* Review real property title documents and prepare title reports and tables showing the ownership history of the property
* Conduct corporate research and identify corporate successors (training will be provided)
* Input data and manage databases
* Translate information obtained from research into charts, graphs, maps, and infographics
* Occasional overnight travel may be required

**Education/Experience**

* Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Arts degree from an accredited university
* Minimum of two years of relevant work experience preferred

**Requirements**

* Hybrid arrangements for Lakewood, CO and Concord, CA.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Detailed, critical, and thoughtful writing and analysis skills
* Knowledge of or experience in environmental information collection, analysis, interpretation and report preparation
* Ability to function as a member of a team and work in a fast-paced environment
* Ability to handle multiple tasks at once and meet deadlines and to adapt quickly and smoothly to changing project requirements
* Proficient in Office 365 and Windows-based applications
* Ability to use software to retrieve, evaluate, and organize information and documents

**Bonus Skills/Certifications**

* Experience with ESRI suite of GIS software is a plus

This position's target hiring rate range is non-exempt, $21.63 to $25.48 per hour, DOQ. This is good faith and a reasonable estimate of the base compensation at the time of posting. Toeroek offers a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, Life, LTD, STD, and 401K.

### **Job Description and Duties**

The mission of the Wildlife Diversity Program is to conserve the rich diversity of California's native wildlife, which includes tens of thousands of terrestrial invertebrates and more than 1,000 species of mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians. The program coordinates statewide conservation activities for native wildlife, including those designated as threatened or endangered pursuant to the California Endangered Species Act.

The Wildlife Diversity Program is hiring one California Endangered Species Act (CESA) Specialist! The incumbent will work independently and as part of a team to provide high level scientific, technical, and policy expertise to support the conservation, management, and monitoring of wildlife species listed under CESA. In this role, the incumbent will lead complex scientific analyses to support emergency listings and provisional candidate determinations under CESA, as well as CESA listing petitions, status reviews, five-year species reviews, recovery planning efforts, and scientific, educational, and management permitting. The incumbent will also support native wildlife conservation through a variety of program efforts which may include analyzing and synthesizing data, developing regulations, reviewing research permits, and developing grant proposals.

Come join us in this exciting and important wildlife conservation work! You willfind additional information about the job in the Duty Statement.

jobs.title: Federal Mine Remediation Lead
jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is seeking a Federal
Mine Remediation Lead
to be based out of any of our locations in the western United States (AZ, CA, CO, MT, NM, NV, OR, UT). This is a full-time role.

This is an exciting growth focused opportunity to build and lead a Mine remediation group. The person in this position will support business development, project execution and have the ability to grow and lead a Mine Remediation practice. We are seeking a leader with major project delivery experience and proven ability to build and lead technical teams in implementing Mine remediation projects, specifically under CERCLA. Preferential consideration will be given to experience on US Federal projects and strong regulatory connections.

As an experienced professional in Mine remediation, you will bring specific technical expertise, sophisticated regulatory understanding, leadership skills, and an entrepreneurial spirit along with a keen interest in evolving and growing the business and mentoring staff. Your demonstrated commitment to safety along with a strong operational understanding of safety risks in mining environments, and ability to mentor employees to support a safe work culture will supplement AECOM’s existing safety culture.

Responsibilities will include:

Working closely with AECOM personnel in United States and Canada to develop and implement Mine remedial solutions for clients in the public and private sector that meet regulatory requirements and protect human health and the environment.
Collaboration with, and coordination of, diverse technical teams including hydrologists, hydrogeologists, geochemists, risk assessors, environmental engineers, geotechnical engineers, civil engineers, water treatment specialists, biologists, revegetation, costing specialists, etc. to develop remedial solutions that meet technical and regulatory requirements.
Reviewing technical work plans and cost estimates; interpreting data; conducting remediation/closure technology evaluations and feasibility studies.
Technical and financial management of projects to meet commitments on budget, quality and schedule.
Development of proposals, project teams and cost estimates.
Delivery of projects, and technical review of reports for regulatory submission (e.g., studies, remediation and closure plans, permit applications, management plans).
Periodically attending site visits to proposed, operating or closed mines in support of client relationship building, proposal development and project delivery.
Business-development activities, including building and maintaining existing and new client relationships, tracking marketing leads and project opportunities, developing proposals and presentations, networking, attending conferences and sharing AECOM’s capabilities with existing and potential clients.
Stakeholder communications, including regulatory communications and client advocacy.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree in relevant engineering (Civil, Geotechnical, Environmental etc.) or science (geology, hydrogeology, environmental etc.) disciplines +8 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or 20+ years of experience
People management experience
Mine remediation experience under CERCLA framework
Proficient technical writing experience for investigation and design reports and regulatory document submissions
Proficient proposals preparation and cost development experience for Mine remediation projects
Experience with US Federal projects, specifically with US Army Corps of Engineers, US Environmental Project Agency, US Department of Interior

Additional Information

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $160000 to $210000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Senior Agrochemical Regulatory Affairs Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description

Inviting bright minds

Do you want to push the boundaries of your profession and develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and empowering culture? We work to create a sustainable future and our inspiring projects and innovative solutions aim to set the standard among our peers. You will join a global company that has been growing successfully since its founding in 1945. Together, we lead and leave a positive impact on societies, companies and people around the world. Ramboll Health Science Spearhead has approx. 360 bright minds globally and you can become one of them in our Australia team contributing to our continued success.

You will join our Environment and Health Business Unit

As our new Senior Consultant, you will have experience and be a subject matter expert in Agrochemical regulations in Australia (APVMA) and New Zealand (EPA and ACVM). You will bring the ability to organize, coordinate and communicate across an interdisciplinary team, engaging externally with technical professionals, and regulatory agencies. You will provide strategic expertise and support the preparation of regulatory submissions for a variety of agrochemical related products in the region. A strong customer service ethic and ability to multitask is vital for this role. You will present a positive “can-do” attitude and be a self-starter within a team of dedicated professionals.

This is a unique opportunity to have a role within the Ramboll Health Science Spearhead to help drive the growth of the agrochemical consulting business in Australia, working with our international team of regulatory and technical experts, while advancing your skills and consulting career. Reporting to the Principal, Health Sciences in Australia your role would be based at one of Ramboll’s Australian Offices.

Your key tasks and responsibility will be:

Support the execution of Product Stewardship and Safety projects with a focus on Australian and New Zealand plant protection registrations
Act as project manager for interdisciplinary agrochemical regulatory projects
Responsible for strategic guidance and translating complex scientific information into regulator-ready submissions.
Advise clients on existing as well as upcoming regulatory obligations (in the fields of environmental, health & safety-related topics)
Developing strategies, market analysis and helping to expand and drive the growth of Ramboll’s agrochemical business in the region.
Active in business development, meeting clients and attending appropriate conferences and seminars to increase Ramboll’s visibility in the region.

Your starting point for constant growth

From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional developments so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is:

Ability to provide strategic advice and determine practical compliance solutions to meet our clients’ commercial aims for their agricultural related products.
Experience leading multi-faceted teams on projects, producing a high-quality work product, on time and within budget
Ability to guide clients through registrations, variations, and label/claims strategies, helping to prepare compliance advice, application dossiers and data-gap analyses.
Staying current with changes in regulatory landscape affecting Ramboll’s clients and maintaining contacts and relationships with regulatory authorities.
Proficiency assessing the impact of new regional regulations on the business and participates in actions to assist our clients in dealing with the implementation of these new regulations.
Strong team player and customer-oriented approach.

Qualifications

Desired skills/experience

A minimum of 7 years’ industry or consulting experience with plant protection product registration in Australia and New Zealand
Scientific background preferably with a degree or higher in agriculture, veterinary medicine, chemistry, biology or a related discipline
Ability to handle multiple tasks and work streams in a fast-paced environment while maintaining outstanding attention to detail and quality of deliverables
Experience/comfort with working in a virtual team with stakeholders across geographies
Ability to support internal and external clients with both technical and strategic consulting services
Experience in business development would be advantageous
Strong written and oral communication skills
Good presentation skills and business sense
Demonstrated problem-solving skills
Possess a drive and personal initiative to keep learning and improving in the chosen field.

Additional Information

Welcome to our Environment & Health division

Ramboll develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions that help increase livability by reducing pollution and restoring natural environments. One of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to manage their most challenging environmental, health and social issues.

Ramboll in Asia Pacific

Ramboll has close to 500 experts working across more than 10 offices in Asia Pacific. We are present in Australia, China, Hong Kong SAR, Malaysia, India, Japan, South Korea and Singapore. Our experts are applying their passion to deliver innovative and sustainable solutions in markets as diverse as Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy and Architecture &, Landscape. Founded in Denmark, Ramboll is a people company. We invite you to contribute to a sustainable future working in an open, collaborative and empowering culture.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in Asia Pacific

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in Asia Pacific has close to 500 people working across ten offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, and Architecture & Landscape.

Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds and characteristics.

Ready to join us?

Please submit your application with your up-to-date CV. We invite diversity in all its forms and encourage applicants from all groups to apply.

Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist Consultant - January Start
jobs.description:
**About Us**
============

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real-world impact.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.

When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

**A Day in the Life**
=====================

Formerly known as Epic Environmental, the Australian arm of Onterris has kept the strong culture we are well known for. The team continues to work closely with clients, building trusted relationships and delivering high-quality outcomes without an overemphasis on KPIs.

Our teams have the opportunity to work alongside industry leaders, auditors, and professionals with vast experience within our industry, while enjoying regular social events and collaborative work that bring the team together. Onterris also supports career development through relevant internal opportunities and individual one-on-one career conversations focused on growth and progression.

We are seeking a Consultant Environmental Scientist to join our growing Contaminated Land and Water team out of our Sydney office. Have the opportunity to work alongside more than 50 land and water professionals across Australia who are actively invested in mentoring, collaboration and your long-term career development.

This role will be responsible for a full range of activities including:

* Planning and delivering field investigations across a variety of sites – including soil, groundwater, and surface water assessments

* Preparing clear and high-quality reports

* Acting as the representative/client contact on site for Onterris

* Attending business development meetings

Supporting project managers and ensuring open and clear communications when in the field  



**Your Expertise and Skills**
=============================

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

* 1-3 years consulting experience in contaminated land

* Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management or related disciplines

* Solid understanding of NSW and national environmental frameworks

* Confidence in the field and an eye for detail and technical excellence

* Open C class drivers licence valid in NSW

Onterris is a leading global environmental solutions company partnering with organizations to solve complex challenges where environmental pressures, regulatory expectations and operational risks intersect. Guided by our mission to advance the way of life without compromising the integrity of our environment, we believe environmental responsibility and human progress are fundamentally connected. Our scientists, engineers, field teams and consultants apply systems thinking that unites science, data and practical expertise to deliver solutions that strengthen our clients’ resilience, mitigate risk and protect the air, water and soil that sustain communities, while uncovering responsible paths forward for planet and progress. For more information, visit www.onterris.com .

We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. We acknowledge that these experiences and perspectives help to enrich our teams and contribute to our ongoing success. We are committed to providing access and reasonable accommodation in our employment for all applicants. For US residents, click here to learn more.

jobs.description:
Westlands Water District is seeking a talented and analytical Water Resources Specialist to help address some of the most complex and impactful water resource challenges facing California today.

This is an exceptional opportunity to play a key role in long-term water supply planning, groundwater management, environmental compliance, and strategic resource initiatives that directly support one of the nation's largest agricultural water districts.

#### **Salary****:**

* **Annual Salary Range:** $100,008 - $200,016.
* **Anticipated Hiring Range:** $100,008 - $150,000 DOQ (Depending on Qualifications).

#### **Location:**

Fresno or Sacramento, California.

#### **Why Join Westlands?**

**As a Water Resources Specialist, you'll work on high-profile projects involving:**

* Central Valley Project (CVP) and State Water Project (SWP) operations.
* Groundwater management and water supply reliability.
* Environmental compliance and permitting.
* Water policy, economic, and technical analyses.
* Hydrologic and operational forecasting.
* Strategic planning and stakeholder coordination.

The ideal candidate is a proactive problem-solver who can translate complex technical and regulatory information into practical recommendations that support critical water management decisions.

#### **Minimum Qualifications:**

Bachelor's degree in Water Resources, Hydrology, Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science, Engineering, Agricultural Science, Public Policy, Economics, Natural Resource Management, or a closely related field, plus three years of professional experience in water resources or a related discipline. A master's degree may substitute for two years of experience.

#### **Outstanding Benefits:**

* CalPERS Retirement.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**Short description**

*From laboratory bench to open air – launch your career in real-world environmental monitoring, with Emission Assessments.*

**Bullet Points**

Located in Bibra Lake, WA (Field-Based Role)  
Full-time | Permanent Position  
Salary: $70,000 – $85,000 + Super

**About the Organisation**

Emission Assessments, a leading environmental services provider, is seeking two motivated scientists to join their team. This is a hands-on, field-based role offering excellent long-term career development and career progression opportunities, within the niche science of air quality testing.

**About the Role**

You will be involved in environmental air monitoring programs, including Industry Stack Emission Testing, Laboratory Practices and Field Odour Surveys. Working in **teams of two**, you will conduct accredited on-site monitoring and sampling at heights using specialised monitoring equipment.

This role combines fieldwork, scientific testing, and technical reporting, making it ideal for science graduates seeking practical experience beyond the laboratory. Technical training in stack emission testing methods is provided for those without experience. Laboratory experience is highly regarded, and those with previous stack testing experience are highly encouraged to apply.

The role operates on an 8 days on / 6 days off roster (initially Monday to Friday during training), based in Perth (Bibra Lake), with approximately 10-hour workdays (9.5 hours plus a 30-minute break). You will have access to a company vehicle for site travel and work across locations in Southwest WA (Pinjarra/Wagerup) and Pilbara mine sites. Initial training is provided on a normal Mon- Fri work week.

Key Responsibilities

* Conduct stack emission testing, odour sampling and laboratory testing, and ambient air/OHS testing
* Be professionally trained in the use of state-of-the-art field and laboratory testing equipment.
* Perform basic chemical laboratory testing and calibrate monitoring equipment
* Maintain accurate field records and compliance documentation
* Complete post-site technical reporting and administration.

**About You**

We are looking for practical, reliable, and motivated individuals who are eager to build a long-term career in environmental science. Ideally, you will have:

* Degree in Environmental Science, Chemistry, or a related discipline
* Strong interest in field-based scientific work
* Prior knowledge of emissions-to-air monitoring highly regarded
* Comfortable working at heights
* Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to liaise with clients and develop professional relationships
* Ability to work autonomously and within a small team
* High attention to detail, and scientific rigour
* Valid Western Australia driver’s license
* Willingness to travel to industrial and mining sites as required

**What the Company Offers**

* Clear career pathway from Environmental Scientist to Advisor
* Self-paced career planning and associated salary increases
* Internationally recognised career certified pathways
* Supported professional development opportunities each year
* Collaborative, supportive team with experienced mentors eager to share knowledge
* Long-term career stability and growth opportunities

**How to Apply**

Click Apply Now to submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your interest in field-based environmental work and why you would be a great fit for this role.

Pay: $70,000.00 – $85,000.00 per year

Work Location: In person
