jobs.title: Water Resources Planner / Scientist
jobs.description:
About Us

We are an award-winning California-based environmental consulting firm with 600+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. Our mission is to deliver practical, science-based environmental and planning solutions that support communities, infrastructure, and natural systems. 

As a people-centric organization, we value collaboration, fairness, and transparency, and are committed to fostering a workplace that supports both personal and professional growth while offering robust career opportunities. We are especially proud of our recent Great Place To Work®
certification, which reflects an independent assessment of our culture and our team-member experiences.  

About The Role 

Rincon is seeking a Water Resources Planner/Scientist
with a background in California water supply/reliability, Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA), geology, hydrology, or hydrogeology to support our growing groundwater and water resources practice across California. This role will focus primarily on SGMA planning and implementation, watershed resilience planning, nature-based and groundwater recharge solutions, water resources planning, and grant funding strategies that move water resource solutions from planning toward implementation. Working with Project Managers, Principals-in-Charge, and interdisciplinary technical teams, you will conduct technical research and analysis; analyze groundwater, hydrologic, water quality, and other water resource data; and contribute to technical reports, planning documents, and funding applications. You will also work with public agency clients and interested parties throughout the planning process, helping to gather and evaluate data, support technical analyses, and communicate findings and recommendations. You will have opportunities to build the technical experience needed for greater responsibility and professional growth. 

You will interact with public agency clients, contribute to community outreach and engagement, and help strengthen client relationships through high-quality project delivery. 

We are looking for a motivated, curious, and collaborative professional who is eager to learn and make a tangible impact. This is an opportunity to build technical expertise, work alongside experienced water resources professionals, and help shape the next generation of sustainable and resilient water management across California. 

How We Collaborate 

This role may offer a hybrid work setup, blending time in the office with remote work as business needs evolve. We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients, and may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office.  
Eligible office locations for this role include Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.  

What You’ll Do 

Support SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, plan updates, groundwater monitoring and data analysis, and evaluation of projects and management actions.  
Contribute to watershed resilience and climate adaptation planning by evaluating groundwater and surface water conditions, hydrology, water supply reliability, drought and climate impacts, and opportunities to improve long-term watershed resilience.  
Evaluate nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, habitat and watershed restoration, stormwater capture, and green infrastructure, using geologic, hydrologic, hydrogeologic, and other technical information.  
Support grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, recharge, watershed resilience, water supply, recycled water, wastewater, stormwater, and other water resource projects, including evaluating project benefits, readiness, and alignment with funding opportunities.  
Contribute to complex water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and permitting and funding applications for water/wastewater facilities. 
Conduct technical research, field investigations, and analysis of groundwater, surface water, water supply, water quality, and related geologic and hydrologic conditions to support water resource planning, permitting, and project implementation.  
Prepare materials to support community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including drafting e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input questions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.   
Analyze and interpret technical data, including groundwater levels, water quality, water use, hydrologic conditions, and other datasets, and translate findings into clear, client-ready technical conclusions and recommendations.  
Prepare technical memoranda, reports, planning documents, presentations, and other materials for public agency clients and interested parties.  
Work collaboratively with hydrogeologists, geologists, engineers, planners, biologists, and other technical specialists and support client and stakeholder meetings, outreach, and project delivery. 

What You’ll Bring 

Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Water Resources, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related technical field.  
Two or more years of relevant professional experience in groundwater, water resources, watershed management, hydrology, environmental planning, or a related field with an emphasis on SGMA and watershed resiliency.  
Foundational understanding of California water resources and interest in groundwater sustainability, water supply/reliability, watershed management, or climate resilience.  
Experience collecting, organizing, analyzing, and interpreting technical or environmental data.  
Strong technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate technical information to a variety of audiences.  
Ability to work collaboratively across technical disciplines, stay organized, and manage multiple assignments and priorities.  
Willingness to learn new technical tools, methods, and regulatory frameworks.  
Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products.  
Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record and willingness to conduct fieldwork and travel as project needs require. 

Nice to Have
Masters degree, coursework, or professional experience in geology, hydrogeology, hydrology, groundwater science, or another water-focused technical discipline.  
Experience with or interest in SGMA implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans, annual reports, periodic evaluations, groundwater monitoring, or implementation of groundwater projects and management actions.  
Experience with groundwater or surface water monitoring, inter-connected surface water studies, groundwater dependent ecosystems, hydrologic analysis, water quality, managed aquifer recharge, groundwater-surface water interactions, or watershed assessment.  
Familiarity with California water laws, regulations, and programs, particularly SGMA and water rights.  
Experience with GIS, groundwater or hydrologic datasets, databases, modeling tools, or other technical analytical applications.  
Experience supporting grant applications, funding strategies, or implementation of groundwater, watershed, climate resilience, or water infrastructure projects.  
Professional certification or licensure, such as Professional Geologist (PG) license, Geologist-in-Training (GIT), Professional Engineer (PE), Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification, or other relevant professional credential, or interest in pursuing professional licensure. 

Investing in You 

The base salary range for this full-time position is $70,000-$95,000
, plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. 

We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards Package designed to support employee well-being, growth, and financial security. Our benefits are designed to offer flexibility and choice, including health coverage options, employer-sponsored insurance, retirement benefits, generous time off, and programs that support learning, growth, and community engagement. 

Explore more about our culture, benefits, and life at Rincon on our Culture and Benefits page. 

Additional Employment Information 

Individuals offered employment must successfully complete a pre-employment drug screening as a condition of employment. Additionally, those hired who may be assigned to federal projects will be subject to further drug testing, including screening for cannabinoids (THC/marijuana), in compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 and other applicable federal regulations, which take precedence over California state and local laws.

About The Role 

Rincon is seeking an experienced Project Manager, Groundwater & Water Resources
to help lead our growing groundwater and water resources practice across California. We are especially interested in candidates who combine strong groundwater and water resources expertise with demonstrated project management and client leadership. California professional licensure, including California Professional Geologist (PG), Certified Engineering Geologist (CEG), or Certified Hydrogeologist (CHG) is preferred for candidates whose background is centered in geology or environmental engineering. 

This role will focus primarily on Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) planning and implementation, watershed resilience, nature-based and groundwater recharge solutions, water resources planning, and grant funding strategies that move water resource solutions from planning through implementation. The successful candidate will combine technical expertise with strong project management and client leadership skills, working alongside groundwater modelers, hydrologists, engineers, planners, environmental scientists, and other specialists. 

This position is well suited for a technical professional ready to take greater ownership of projects and client relationships while continuing to deepen their expertise in groundwater sustainability and integrated water resources management.

How We Collaborate 

This role may offer a hybrid work setup, blending time in the office with remote work as business needs evolve. We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients, and may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office.  

Eligible office locations for this role include Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.  

What You’ll Do 

Lead and manage SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans (GSPs) and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, monitoring programs, evaluation of sustainable management criteria, groundwater projects and management actions, and adaptive management strategies. 
Evaluate complex groundwater and water resource conditions using hydrogeologic, hydrologic, water quality, land use, and climate information, including groundwater levels and storage, water budgets, groundwater-surface water interactions, groundwater dependent ecosystems, and basin sustainability issues. 
Lead or support watershed resilience and climate adaptation efforts, integrating groundwater, surface water, water supply, land use, climate vulnerability, and other technical information to develop practical long-term resilience strategies. 
Evaluate and advance nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, stormwater capture, watershed restoration, green infrastructure, and related water infrastructure, working with multidisciplinary technical teams to assess feasibility, benefits, constraints, and implementation considerations. 
Lead development of grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, watershed resilience, recharge, water supply, and other water resource projects, helping clients align technically sound projects with available funding and move priority projects toward implementation. 
Direct and integrate technical work performed by multidisciplinary teams, including groundwater modelers, hydrologists, engineers, geologists, environmental scientists, GIS professionals, and other specialists; review technical analyses and work products for quality, consistency, and defensibility. 
Lead development and QA/QC of complex, multidisciplinary water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and funding applications. 
Lead development of water supply and demand forecasting models using excel-based decision-support tools, addressing water demand factors, passive and active conservation savings, climate change impacts on water use and supply availability, wastewater and return flow generation, and recycled water/non-potable connections.  
Manage projects and client relationships, including scopes, budgets, schedules, contracts, subcontractors, deliverables, meetings, and multidisciplinary project teams across multiple concurrent assignments. 
Lead planning and facilitation of community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input sessions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.   
Communicate complex technical information clearly through technical reports and memoranda, presentations, workshops, public meetings, and discussions with Groundwater Sustainability Agencies, water districts, municipalities, state agencies, stakeholders, and other clients. 
Support proposals, client development, and other business development efforts while mentoring and developing early- and mid-career water resources professionals. 

What You’ll Bring 

Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Geological Engineering, Civil or Environmental Engineering, Water Resources, or a closely related technical field. 
Five or more years of relevant professional experience in groundwater, hydrogeology, hydrology, water resources, SGMA planning and implementation, watershed management, or related technical consulting. 
Demonstrated technical understanding of groundwater systems and hydrogeologic principles, with the ability to interpret and critically evaluate groundwater, hydrologic, water quality, and other water resource data. 
Experience with SGMA or technically comparable groundwater management work, including GSP implementation, groundwater assessments, monitoring, water budgets, sustainability evaluations, or projects and management actions. 
Experience managing projects, including scopes, schedules, budgets, technical teams, deliverables, and client communications. 
Ability to understand and work effectively with groundwater models, water budgets, and other technical analyses and modeling outputs, even if numerical modeling is not the candidate's primary specialty. 
Strong technical writing, QA/QC, presentation, and communication skills. 
Experience working directly with public agencies, water agencies, or other water resource clients. 
Working knowledge of California groundwater and water resource regulations and programs. 
Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and work effectively across technical disciplines. 
Valid driver's license with a clean driving record and willingness to travel and participate in field activities as project needs require. 

Nice to Have
Certified Hydrogeologist (CHG) or Certified Engineering Geologist (CEG). 
Master's degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Geological Engineering, Water Resources, or a closely related technical discipline. 
Significant experience implementing SGMA, including GSPs or Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, sustainable management criteria, water budgets, monitoring networks, or projects and management actions. 
Experience interpreting groundwater model results and working directly with modelers on model development, calibration, scenarios, water budgets, or decision-support analyses. 
Experience evaluating groundwater-surface water interactions, managed aquifer recharge, subsidence, groundwater dependent ecosystems, water quality, or other SGMA sustainability issues. 
Experience developing and implementing monitoring programs, field investigations, or hydrogeologic studies. 
Experience with GIS, groundwater databases, hydrologic or groundwater modeling tools, or other technical analytical platforms. 
Experience developing successful grant applications or funding strategies for groundwater, watershed, climate resilience, or water infrastructure projects. 
Experience developing water supply and demand forecast models to support long-range water resources planning efforts. 
Demonstrated experience leading client meetings, workshops, technical discussions, and public or stakeholder presentations. 
Experience developing scopes and budgets, preparing proposals, supporting business development, and developing long-term client relationships. 
Experience mentoring geologists, hydrologists, scientists, engineers, or other technical professionals.

, plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

jobs.title: Service Center Supervisor- Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West, Bend, OR
jobs.description:
Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

Job Description

Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West is seeking a Service Center Supervisor to join our team in Bend OR!

Responsibilities

Oversee all activities and employees of the location
Project management of all received samples and projects as needed
Analyze microbiology and inorganic testing on potable and non-potable water samples
Perform monthly environmental testing (water, surfaces, air) and annual calibrations
Receive and log potable water and non-potable water samples from clients
Create microbiological and chemical projects and reports and corresponding invoices
Prepare various media types for sample analysis
Submit all compliance drinking water to Oregon State Heath Authority and EPA as needed
Answer and respond to all client correspondence via phone and email
Schedule all equipment calibration and maintain diligent records
Schedule all sample collections performed by the location
Consult public on testing and sampling procedures
Consult water systems and utilities on testing and sampling procedures
Maintain laboratory supply inventory
Maintain all SOPs and training documents
Maintain all NELAP certification requirements including but not limited to: proficiency testing, internal audits, logbook audits, on-site audits by accreditation body and audit responses
Act as onsite Quality Control Officer
Maintain and organize clients chemical and sampling schedules along with bottle orders and personalized CoCs.
Ability to analyze samples on weekends, holidays and on call, as needed

Qualifications

Education/Experience

Associate's degree in chemistry, microbiology, biology, environmental science, or a related physical, chemical, or environmental science discipline required. Candidates must have:
A minimum of 16 semester credit hours in chemistry and at least two (2) years of experience performing environmental chemical analyses, and/or
A minimum of 4 semester credit hours in general microbiology and at least one (1) year of experience performing microbiological analyses, including drinking water microbiology testing.

2 years customer experience preferred

Skills/Qualifications

Aseptic technique
Excellent customer service
Reliable, timely and punctual
Multitasking with strong time management
Work within strict time requirements of microbiology tests
Excellent documentation, computer and organization skills
Must be able to communicate effectively with lab personnel and clients
Previous knowledge of environmental testing and compliance regulations is desired
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship

Additional Information

Position is full-time salaried, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm with possibility of longer hours and weekends as needed.

The salary range for this position is $65,000 - $70,000 annually.

Candidates within a commutable distance to Bend, OR are encouraged to apply.

Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com

We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us!
We are well on our way to achieving our objective of carbon neutrality by 2025, through a combination of emission reduction and compensation initiatives. We encourage our laboratory leaders to make sustainable changes at their local level, and in addition to their initiatives we also count on our dedicated carbon reduction team to help us to achieve this goal!

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Company description
: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

jobs.description:
We're seeking an Environmental Specialist to work for a major client in the LA Area, a fast-growing environmental services firm with a healthy pipeline of projects for the next 7+ years.

Responsibilities:

Conduct comprehensive regulatory research to ensure clients are informed of the latest environmental standards and compliance requirements.

Collaborate with clients to facilitate adherence to federal, state, and local environmental regulations.

Prepare and submit detailed environmental compliance plans, permits, and reports related to air quality, hazardous waste management, spill prevention, stormwater, and wastewater.

Liaise with regulatory agencies and maintain proactive communication with clients during field assessments and site visits.

Requirements:

Bachelors Degree in HSE/Environmental or Equivalent Experience.

A minimum of 7 years of professional experience in environmental science with a strong emphasis on regulatory compliance.

Oil and Gas / Energy sector experience is a plus

jobs.title: Security Remediation Manager - Global Security Organization
jobs.description:
Responsibilities

The mission of TikTok's Global Security Organization is to build and earn trust by reducing risk and securing our businesses and products. Also known as "GSO", this team is the foundation of our efforts to keep TikTok safe, secure, and operating at scale for over 1 billion people around the world. We work to ensure that the TikTok platform is safe and secure, that our users' experience and their data remains safe from external or internal threats, and that we comply with global regulations wherever TikTok operates.

Trust is one of TikTok's biggest initiatives, and security is integral to our success. In whatever ways users interact with us — whether they're watching videos on their For You page, interacting with a Live video, or buying products on TikTok Shop — GSO protects their data and privacy, so they can have a secure and trustworthy experience.

The Security Posture Management (SPM) program is responsible for providing a centralized view of security incident-driven issues across the organization and driving consistent, risk-based remediation across teams.
As a Remediation Manager, you will own the end-to-end lifecycle of security issues from intake and prioritization through remediation and closure. You will partner with security domain teams, engineering teams, infrastructure teams, and business stakeholders to ensure high-priority security risks are clearly owned and remediated within defined timelines.
This role requires a strong combination of security knowledge, program management, data-driven decision-making, and cross-functional influence.

Responsibilities
- Manage security issues identified across multiple sources, including security incidents, vulnerability management, penetration testing, risk assessments, insider risk, and other security programs.
- Establish, customize, and maintain centralized issue tracking and remediation management systems, and continuously enhance automated posture management processes — including findings intake, remediation ticketing, ownership assignment, action planning, severity calibration, escalation, and closure — to streamline operations across Incident Response, Vulnerability Management, and other security domains.
- Partner with security domain teams to conduct root-cause analyses, identify systemic control gaps, and co-design sustainable remediation solutions that translate security findings into executable projects and initiatives.
- Drive end-to-end remediation of high-priority security issues with security domain teams, security BP, engineering, infrastructure, IT, and other stakeholder teams.
- Define clear remediation strategies, action plans, milestones, accountable owners, and target completion dates based on risk and business impact.
- Proactively identify and resolve remediation blockers, cross-team dependencies, ownership gaps, and competing priorities.
- Escalate overdue, blocked, or high-risk issues through appropriate governance and leadership channels when necessary.
- Validate remediation implementation and supporting evidence, partnering with security SMEs to confirm that identified risks have been effectively addressed and closure criteria are met.
- Develop security posture dashboards and reporting to provide clear visibility into remediation roadmaps, progress, key milestones, and overall risk reduction.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualification(s)
- Experience managing security findings or remediation programs across multiple technical teams.
- Strong understanding of common security risks across areas such as cloud, infrastructure, identity, endpoints, applications, and vulnerabilities.
- Demonstrated ability to drive complex cross-functional initiatives without direct authority.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to prioritize issues based on risk and business impact.
- Experience developing security metrics, dashboards, or executive-level reporting.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical security risks to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualification(s)
- 5+ years of experience in cybersecurity, security program management, vulnerability management, security operations, risk management, or related fields.
- Experience building or operating centralized security issue management or security posture management programs.
- Experience with security domains such as incident response, vulnerability management, threat intelligence, etc.
- Experience with managing cross-functional remediation programs across multiple regions.
- Understanding of security frameworks such as NIST CSF, CIS Controls, ISO 27001, or related standards.
- Experience with root-cause analysis and identifying systemic security control gaps.
- Experience using automation, data analytics, or AI to improve security operations and remediation workflows.

About TikTok

TikTok is the leading destination for short-form mobile video. At TikTok, our mission is to inspire creativity and bring joy. TikTok's global headquarters are in Los Angeles and Singapore, and we also have offices in New York City, London, Dublin, Paris, Berlin, Dubai, Jakarta, Seoul, and Tokyo.​

Why Join Us

Inspiring creativity is at the core of TikTok's mission. Our innovative product is built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Together, we create value for our communities, inspire creativity and bring joy - a mission we work towards every day.​
We strive to do great things with great people. We lead with curiosity, humility, and a desire to make impact in a rapidly growing tech company. Every challenge is an opportunity to learn and innovate as one team. We're resilient and embrace challenges as they come. By constantly iterating and fostering an "Always Day 1" mindset, we achieve meaningful breakthroughs for ourselves, our company, and our users. When we create and grow together, the possibilities are limitless. Join us.​
​
Diversity & Inclusion​
TikTok is committed to creating an inclusive space where employees are valued for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. Our platform connects people from across the globe and so does our workplace. At TikTok, our mission is to inspire creativity and bring joy. To achieve that goal, we are committed to celebrating our diverse voices and to creating an environment that reflects the many communities we reach. We are passionate about this and hope you are too.​

TikTok Accommodation

If you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation, please reach out to us at https://tinyurl.com/RA-request​

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Remediation Analytics & Governance
jobs.description:
About The Role

This is a highly influential leadership opportunity sitting at the intersection of customer remediation, data, governance and regulatory compliance. As Senior Manager - Remediation Analytics & Governance, you will lead the Data Analytics team supporting the Customer Remediation, Product Governance and Quality function, delivering enterprise reporting, dashboards, customer insights, trend analysis and early warning risk indicators that help us make informed decisions and achieve better outcomes for our customers.

You will be required to continue to strengthen BOQ Group’s Customer Remediation Policy, Standard and supporting governance framework to ensure our approach remains consistent, sustainable and aligned with regulatory expectations at an enterprise level. Working closely with leaders across Risk, Compliance, Regulatory Affairs, Customer Relations, Legal and the broader business, you will provide thoughtful oversight and constructive challenge across centrally managed and business-led remediation programs.

Your role will report to the Head of Customer Remediation, Product Governance & Quality providing governance support associated to sustainable compliance and customer outcomes specific to customer remediation.

What makes this opportunity particularly exciting is its reach. You will be close enough to the work to understand the detail, while having the visibility and influence to shape customer remediation practices across the enterprise. It is meaningful work with real customer impact, supported by a people-centred environment where care, accountability, thoughtful challenge and clear decision-making work together.

About You

You are an experienced leader who brings strong knowledge of banking, financial services, customer remediation, conduct risk, compliance, governance or regulatory programs.

You understand ASIC RG277 and RG274, the Three Lines of Defence model, risk appetite frameworks, controls and enterprise risk governance, and you know how to translate these requirements into practical frameworks that people can understand and apply.

You are equally comfortable working with data and people. You bring sound judgement, curiosity and the confidence to challenge constructively, always keeping customer outcomes and sustainable compliance in sight.

You will have demonstrated experience developing and embedding enterprise policies, standards, governance frameworks and reporting, along with people leadership capability to bring multidisciplinary teams together around shared outcomes. Experience engaging with external legal advisers or regulatory bodies will be highly regarded, as will qualifications in business, law, risk, data analytics or a related discipline.

Most importantly, you are looking for more than a role where you simply maintain what already exists - you want the opportunity to improve how things work, influence decisions across a whole bank and grow through meaningful contribution. At BOQ Group, you will be trusted to stay close to the work, think beyond functional boundaries and help create better, more sustainable outcomes for our customers.

Bring your expertise. Shape better customer outcomes. Build what’s next with BOQ Group.

About Us

BOQ Group is a truly unique group of challenger brands with a purpose – to provide a genuine alternative to Australian financial services for customers and employees.

Our family of brands (Bank of Queensland (BOQ), ME Bank, Virgin Money Australia, BOQ Specialist), each come with their own defined customer audience and brand personality, but share one goal – to build social capital through banking. That’s creating trust with customers, exploring staff potential and believing that tiny gestures and big ideas can change the world for communities.

BOQ Group’s inclusive vision is to foster a workspace that values and leverages difference and creates new possibilities, a place where our people feel confident to bring their best selves to work every day. We embrace difference and believe that our workforce should reflect the customers and communities that we serve.

In 2023, we successfully implemented an innovative Reconciliation Plan, driving positive change and promoting inclusivity across BOQ Group.

Our perks

At BOQ Group, we are passionate about creating an exceptional work environment that nurtures both your professional and personal growth.

Benefits

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to enhance your well-being, provide financial security, and foster a sense of community and inclusion. Here are just some of the fantastic perks you can enjoy as part of our team:

Flexible working arrangement - Balance your work and personal life with ease.
Discounted financial products - Enjoy exclusive rates on our financial services across the Group.
Salary sacrificing options - Maximise your take-home pay with our salary packaging options.
Paid parental leave with no minimum requirements - Spend quality time with your new family member without any worries.
Purchase additional annual leave - Need more time off? You can buy extra leave days.
Discounted private health insurance plan - Take care of your health with our special rates.
Employee Assistance Program (EAP) - Access confidential support for personal and professional challenges for you and your family
Access to employee network groups - Connect with peers through our First Nations Reconciliation, LGBTQIA+, Multicultural, Gender, Early Careers, and accessibility groups.
Pride in Diversity membership: We are proud members of Pride in Diversity and actively participate in the Australian Workplace Equality Index.

We are committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels valued and supported. Join us and be part of a company that truly cares about its people and community!

How To Apply

To apply for this role, follow the links.

BOQ Group is committed to diversity and an inclusive workforce. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People are encouraged to apply.

We celebrate, value and include people of all backgrounds, gender and expressions, sexualities, cultures, bodies and abilities. When you apply, you are welcome to tell us the pronouns you use and please let us know any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process.

jobs.title: Toxicologist
jobs.description:
Accountable for leading the non-clinical development process through designing and implementing non-clinical strategies for successful development of the company’s lead molecules across all stages of development. Responsible for non-clinical department activities which comprise toxicology, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics (DMPK), bioanalytical assay validation and conduct, and biomarkers. The ability to execute and lead sound science-based non-clinical development strategies to support clinical development is a crucial part of this position. Responsible for establishing and culturing interactions with other key groups such as Discovery, Regulatory, and Clinical Pharmacology. 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Lead and provide guidance to the non-clinical group in all matters related to safety assessment, drug disposition studies and bioanalysis related to compounds in all stages of drug development.
Provide scientific guidance to senior management on key issues related to non-clinical development through informal discussions and formal meetings including Program Leadership Teams, Development Review Group, Science Committees and Board Meetings.
Critically evaluate and interpret results of scientific studies and contribute to appropriate sections of INDs, NDAs, IBs and other regulatory documents.
Design and prepare summaries pertaining to toxicology and nonclinical studies to support investigational new drug and new drug application programs.
Assist in resolving nonclinical safety issues through the establishment of novel protocols to solve experimental questions.
Direct and give design input for internal/external toxicology, drug disposition and pharmacology studies.
Serve as key point person to coordinate early activities for a successful transition of nonclinical research to clinical settings.
Provide nonclinical and toxicological updates through presentations to project teams and management as requested.
Coordinate authoring of other preclinical documents – e.g., non-clinical PK summaries and nonclinical pharmacology summaries used in regulatory submissions.
Manage non-clinical development staff including external vendors.
Prepare budget proposals and manage department expenses accordingly.
Assist in the review of vendor contracts and legal agreements as appropriate.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS:

Ph.D. or M.S. in biological science with emphasis in toxicology preferred.
Professional membership (e.g, SOT or ACT) is desirable.
Experience in the writing and review of regulatory documents (both IND and NDA/BLA) and prior experience with US and international regulatory agency interactions.
Ability to build productive cross-functional collaborations both internally and externally is essential.
Sustained record of achievement in leading toxicology research programs supporting safety assessment of drug development candidates is required.
Demonstrated strong decision making and complex data analysis and interpretation relating to drug development.
Strong communication, organizational and interpersonal skills to work within a matrix setting.

Salary range- 100-140K

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist II
jobs.description:
Job Title: Environmental Scientist II

Location: Pleasanton, CA

Description/Job Summary

POSITION DESCRIPTION

HGL is currently seeking an Environmental Scientist II to support environmental restoration projects for federal government clients including USEPA, USACE, USAF, NASA, and various agencies across the United States and territories. Projects commonly involve investigation and remediation of sites with groundwater or soil impacted by emerging contaminants (PFAS), chlorinated solvents, and petroleum compounds as well as abandoned mine lands.

The Environmental Scientist II will work out of our Pleasanton, CA office, unless on field assignments. This role requires travel of up to 50%, primarily within the Western US, but may include occasional travel across the US.

Responsibilities/Duties

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Ensuring field operations are conducted in a safe manner in accordance with project specific Site Safety and Health Plans / Health and Safety Plans.
Participating in field teams for collection of water, soil, soil vapor, surface water and sediment samples utilizing various sampling techniques.
Performing / conducting field subcontractor oversight inclusive of drilling, monitoring well construction, waste transportation and disposal, and heavy equipment operation.
Contributing to the preparation of work plans and project deliverables (e.g., UFP-QAPPs, RI Reports, SSHP/HASPs, power point presentations, and technical memoranda).
Assisting with data entry, analysis, and interpretation of environmental data using statistical and visualization tools.
Assisting with proposals, cost estimates, and subcontractor procurement.
Potentially assisting with remedial system operations and maintenance services.
Managing / Leading field teams collecting general field data and completing environmental sampling.
Utilize approved digital and AI-assisted tools, where appropriate, to support technical documentation, data analysis, project communications, and workflow efficiency.

Minimum Requirements

WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

2+ years of directly related experience in the environmental industry .
Strong technical writing and documentation experience with prior experience contributing to the preparation of technical reports, memoranda, and work plans.
Previous experience with environmental investigations including various groundwater, soil, and surface water/sediment methodologies.
Experience with monitoring well drilling, logging, installation and sampling; developing boring logs and review/interpretation of geological boring logs.
Ability to work within a team environment with corporate, project, and technical management staff.
Excellent interpersonal communication skills (both written and oral) including the ability to comfortably engage with varying levels of leadership, subcontractors, internal and external stakeholders.
Proficient in MS Word, MS Excel, and other MS Office applications.
Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Environmental Science, Hydrogeology, Geophysics, Geological/Geotechnical Engineering or a related field.
Demonstrated ability to learn and adopt new technologies and digital tools to improve project delivery and operational efficiency.

Desired Qualifications

WHAT YOU NEED TO STAND OUT – Preferred, not required

Master’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science, Geophysics, Geological/geotechnical Engineering or a related field.
HAZWOPER 40-hour training.
Experience as a Task Manager or Field Team Leader for environmental investigations.
Knowledge and experience of CERCLA, DoD, DOE, EPA, and/or RCRA projects.
PFAS sampling or remediation experience.
Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve technical writing, data analysis, research, visualization, or project delivery efficiency.

Physical & Environmental Requirements

PHYSICAL & COGNITIVE REQUIREMENTS

Ability to lift/move/relocate items up to 50 lbs.
Prolonged sitting up to 70% of the time.
Prolonged standing up to 70% of the time.
Walking over uneven or mountainous terrain.
Viewing computer screen for extended periods.
Ability to interpret and analyze visual data (maps, graphs, warning indicators, etc.).
Driving a company or personal vehicle.
Complex problem solving and decision making.
Reading and interpreting technical documents or regulations.
Communicating effectively with clients, team members, and stakeholders.
Managing competing deadlines and shifting priorities.

Work Environment Requirements

Must be able to work outdoors in adverse weather conditions (heat, cold, rain, snow, etc.).
Must be able to travel up to 50% of the year.
May work in environments with loud noises, dust, or hazardous materials.
Must wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).
Office work environment.
Potential for longer days up to 12 hours in duration.

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.

Details

Work Schedule
HGL office work is dictated by a 5-day work week; however, fieldwork schedules will deviate based on job requirements and may require longer hours and weekends.

Office Type
:
In-office when not in the field or traveling

Travel:
50%

FLSA Classification:
Exempt

A favorable pre-hire drug test and physical are required. All positions are subject to a pre-hire education and driving record verification.

This specific role supports a U.S. Federal government contract which requires employees engaged on this contract to be U.S. citizens.

MORE ABOUT HGL AND THE OPPORTUNITY

At HGL, we share a drive and vision to restore natural resources and provide ongoing stewardship of our environment to benefit present and future generations. We believe that we can make a difference in improving the world we live in through collaboration, teamwork, and a positive work environment. This unites and empowers us to strive for excellence in all our endeavors.

Hgl - Who We Are

The exceptional quality of our people is key to our strength. We value our employees as individuals and as important members of our team. We offer a work environment that is flexible, inclusive, and dedicated to creating a sustainable future. By cultivating a culture of innovation, we’re able to adapt and augment our services to solve complex environmental and natural resources challenges.

Projects at HGL primarily span the United States and its territories, tackling problems associated with emerging contaminants (like PFAS), radiological contamination, and military munitions, along with chemical contamination in groundwater, surface water, sediments, and soil.

With over 550 employees, HGL is large enough to execute high-profile projects, but small enough to develop personal working environments with our talented team members. By joining HGL, you will be working toward restoring the environment and protecting our future.

HGL - WE INVEST IN YOU

It’s not just a job, it’s your career. HGL provides career growth opportunities via mentoring, training, education, and support for your certifications and licenses. Achieve your career goals and help HGL achieve its mission of restoring the environment to beneficial use for our clients and communities.

### **Department Information**

The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.

  

The Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch (MDFS) is responsible for ensuring that milk, dairy products, and products resembling milk products (PRMPs) are safe, unadulterated, and properly labeled to safeguard public health. jobs.title: Environmental Health Specialist II
jobs.description:
About FACS

At FACS, our mission is to make environments safer and healthier for the people who live and work in them. As one of the nation's leading environmental health consulting firms, we help organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. We are built on purpose, partnership, and performance, delivering measurable impact with every client engagement.
Our Values

We live our mission through three core values:
People First:
Support our team and clients, promote professional growth, and value collaboration.
Integrity of the Science:
Deliver accurate, reliable results through objective, evidence-based practices.
Client Relationships for Life:
Build long-term partnerships and help clients address environmental health challenges.

Why Join Us

At FACS, you’ll contribute meaningful work that helps organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. You’ll join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and mission-driven team that values scientific integrity, strong client relationships, and professional growth.
Ranked "Best Places to Work" for five consecutive years, we invest in your success through training, mentorship, and support for professional certifications, so you can grow, thrive, and build a career with lasting impact.
Curious to see what we do? Meet our team at FACS Experts.
About the Role

The Environmental Health Specialist II is a hands-on, field-based role supporting industrial hygiene, asbestos, and microbial (mold and moisture) projects. The Specialist performs on-site surveys, inspections, assessments, abatement oversight, air sampling, clearances, and project monitoring, and prepares clear, accurate written field reports.
This role may take the lead on assigned projects when Environmental Health Specialists or field technicians are assigned, coordinating closely with the Project Manager, contractors, and clients. Local travel to client and project sites is a regular part of the role.
Fieldwork and Reporting

Perform on-site surveys, inspections, assessments, abatement oversight, and monitoring for industrial hygiene, asbestos, and microbial projects.
Perform asbestos air sampling, clearances, and on-site analysis of air samples while adhering to quality-control requirements.
Prepare written field reports and maintain acceptable report turnaround times.
Identify and secure necessary tools and equipment for assigned projects.
Maintain internal QA/QC compliance.

Project Coordination and Communication

Take the lead on projects when Environmental Health Specialists or field technicians are assigned.
Communicate vital project information to Project Managers to support coordination and progress tracking.
Serve as a liaison between the client, Project Manager, and contractor.
Report project progress and provide technical input to the Project Manager.
Obtain and track project numbers for accurate record-keeping.
Adapt the scope of work in the field as needed to accommodate actual conditions or changes during project progression.

Compliance and Contractor Oversight

Review contractor personnel certifications, medical clearances, and other required documentation to ensure compliance with abatement requirements.
Act as a point of contact and meet with regulatory agents in the event of surprise site inspections.

Team Development and Professional Growth

Assist with training and mentoring junior staff.
Attend required internal and external technical training.
Maintain technical certifications.

Experience

Minimum of two years of experience as a field technician conducting field surveys, inspections, assessments, or asbestos-related monitoring work.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, and ability to quickly learn new software and systems.

Education and Credentials

Bachelor of Science in industrial hygiene, health and safety, biological science, physical science, or a related field—or equivalent relevant experience.
Current California Site Surveillance Technician (CSST) certification required.

Preferred Experience

Experience with asbestos abatement monitoring, air sampling, clearances, or indoor environmental quality work.
Experience serving as a field lead or coordinating with contractors, clients, or junior staff.

Physical & Work Requirements

Physical ability to stoop, kneel, climb, crawl, walk, and stand for extended periods in varied work environments while performing sampling activities
Ability to lift and carry equipment weighing up to 50 lbs.
Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer for documentation and reporting
Must be able to pass a background check, annual medical examinations, and OSHA-required respirator fit tests
Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance
Ability to travel locally to assigned client and project sites

Compensation and Rewards

Competitive base salary with performance-based bonus structure tied to individual and team achievements
Comprehensive benefits package, including:
Medical coverage with 100% company-paid premiums for employees and their families, plus 50% of the annual deductible covered by the company
401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions
Vision and dental plan options
Flexible Spending Accounts (health care and dependent care)
Company-sponsored programs including Employee Assistance Program, life and disability insurance, Rocket Lawyer legal services, and mobile phone plan with Verizon
Voluntary benefits options including supplemental life insurance for employees and dependents, short-term disability, hospital, accident, and pet insurance
Generous PTO (3 weeks accrual), paid holidays, volunteer days, and floating holiday
Tuition Reimbursement Program to promote higher education
Paid training and certifications to support career advancement
Incentive Bonus Plan and Donation Matching Program

Wage Transparency

Pay for this position is based on a number of factors including geographic location, relevant knowledge, skills, and experience.

If you are a certified CSST or experienced environmental health field professional who enjoys hands-on fieldwork, asbestos and microbial projects, and supporting clients and project teams, we encourage you to apply. This is an opportunity to take on field leadership, develop technically, and grow within a specialized environmental health consulting practice.

jobs.description:
About Children's Ground

Children’s Ground is a First Nations organisation. The Children’s Ground Approach is designed and delivered through the leadership of First Nations people. We are committed to systems change to ensure dignity, justice and equity for all children and families. Our work focuses on national reform as well as evidencing a new way of working.

The Children’s Ground Approach is a whole of community, whole of life approach. We privilege First Nations knowledge systems and practice. Over the course of a generation, led by local expertise, we create and deliver an integrated system that is centred on learning, development and wellbeing that responds to the child and their family through the key transition points from pre-birth to young adulthood.

Our approach recognises the cultural, social, and economic strength of our communities. We build on this over a generation to ensure a future for our children and grandchildren that gives them freedom, opportunity and rights to their culture and identity.

Children’s Ground operates in Central Australia and across the Top End, with support provided by a Melbourne-based Shared Services team.

About The Role

This position will provide services to Central Australia, across five different communities in and around Mparntwe – Alice Springs. The Environmental Health Coordinator will work within a multi-disciplinary team with particular focus on delivering Environmental Health Promotion under the Children’s Ground Family Health and Wellbeing Framework Health in the Hands of the People Utnenge, Tyerrtye, Mwerre Atnyenetyeke Iltye Tyerrtye Urrperle–kenhenge to improve health and wellbeing outcomes for communities. T

The Environmental Health Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing two Orange Sky Laundry trucks, the planned schedule of service delivery across various locations in Mparntwe and staff attached to the trucks in community. Environmental health support is also provided through provision of access to cleaning equipment and other items that will support community members to maintain their homes and support security of tenure. Staff training, advocacy and increasing tenant agency are expected outcomes of the position.

Key Responsibilities

Children’s Ground Family Health Model

Work within the Children’s Ground Family Health and Wellbeing Framework Health in the Hands of the People, to improve health and wellbeing outcomes for the communities we work with.
With the community, develop, assess, and monitor environmental health needs, and manage and implement responses to create improved health and wellbeing outcomes for First Nations people across the region
Ensure that the Environmental Health team is accessible to all First Nations people in the communities where we work.
Support the delivery of health and wellbeing information and services in first language and support local cultural knowledge, life, and lore.
Work with the Learning and Wellbeing Team to support the integration of health and wellbeing into daily learning and development initiatives across CG.

Oversight and delivery of key components of the Family health and Wellbeing Framework including:

Ensure OrangeSky laundry trucks and Environmental Health trailers are deployed Monday to Friday. Support attendees to manage the assets appropriately and facilitate their utilisation across the communities.
Roster and supervise laundry and environmental health trailers with local First Nations people in the community.
Development and implementation of environmental health promotion initiatives as identified and prioritised by community, including but not limited to: Laundry, House cleans and Yard Cleans

Local Community Agency and respect for local cultural knowledge and life

Meet regularly with local First Nations families to discuss local aspirations, to inform directions and responsibilities of Children’s Ground.
Ensure participants have access to information and services that will assist them to maintain their tenancies or address tenancy issues.
Encourage and support First Nations, valuing their ideas, strategies and aspirations
Provide mentoring, management, and guidance to staff to develop professional, trusting, and respectful relationships with people in the region.

Our Commitment and Working Environment

Our work is grounded in deep engagement with First Nations communities and in contributing to long‑term systems change. This environment is rich, relational and meaningful, but can also present challenges that affect timelines that may impact your work - including the need to work respectfully to cultural protocols, respond to community priorities, and navigate complex service systems. Team members must be comfortable working in a flexible, adaptive way that honours community‑led processes while managing competing demands.

Children’s Ground is a Child Safe Organisation, placing children’s safety and wellbeing at the centre of our values, we follow the National Principals for Child Safe Organisations.

At Children’s Ground, culture, language, and First Nations knowledge systems are at the forefront of everything we do. We are committed to creating a walking-together environment that is culturally safe, inclusive, and deeply respectful of diversity. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, individuals from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and people living with a disability. We are a flexible workplace and provide reasonable adjustments throughout our recruitment process—if you require support or alternative formats to apply, please reach out to jennifer.wallace@childrensground.org.au.

To ensure our workforce reflects the families we partner with, the filling of this position is intended to constitute a special measure under section 8(1) of the Racial Discrimination Act 1975. While this role is open to all applicants who share our vision for systemic change, applications from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander candidates will be strongly prioritised. We highly value lived experience, cultural expertise, and deep connections to community alongside professional skills.

We will be reviewing applications on a rolling basis and may close this ad early if we find the right fit. If you are interested in joining us, we warmly encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist III / Senior Environmental Scientist
to join our Environmental Remediation Practice in Richmond, California
.

The successful candidate will provide technical leadership and project coordination for environmental investigation, remediation, groundwater monitoring, compliance, and emergency response projects throughout Northern California and the western United States. This position will support a diverse portfolio of industrial, energy, transportation, municipal, and commercial clients while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams of scientists, engineers, geologists, and technical specialists.

The ideal candidate will have strong experience managing environmental field programs, coordinating subcontractors and laboratories, overseeing health and safety compliance, managing environmental data, and preparing technical and regulatory deliverables.

This position will be based in Richmond, California, with opportunities to support projects throughout Northern California and the western United States.

Responsibilities

Technical and Project Leadership

Lead environmental investigation, monitoring, remediation, and compliance projects from planning through execution.
Coordinate field schedules, staffing, subcontractors, laboratory services, equipment, and site logistics.
Develop and implement work plans, sampling plans, health and safety documentation, and project-specific field procedures.
Support project managers with project planning, budgeting, scheduling, resource forecasting, and client communications.
Identify project risks and develop solutions to achieve project objectives while maintaining quality, schedule, and budget commitments.

Groundwater Monitoring and Remediation

Plan and oversee groundwater, soil, sediment, and waste characterization programs.
Manage groundwater monitoring events and environmental sampling activities.
Coordinate remedial investigations, corrective action programs, groundwater treatment systems, and in-situ remediation efforts.
Evaluate environmental data and support development of remedial strategies and technical recommendations.
Ensure field activities are performed in accordance with project requirements and applicable regulations.

Environmental Compliance

Support environmental compliance programs for industrial, infrastructure, remediation, and construction projects.
Conduct environmental inspections, audits, and compliance assessments.
Monitor project activities for compliance with permits, mitigation measures, Environmental Protection Plans (EPPs), and Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs).
Coordinate with regulatory agencies, contractors, and stakeholders to support permitting and environmental compliance objectives.

Health and Safety

Implement and enforce site-specific Health and Safety Plans (HASPs), Job Safety Analyses (JSAs), and company safety procedures.
Lead daily safety meetings, hazard assessments, and pre-task planning activities.
Support atmospheric monitoring, radiological monitoring, confined-space activities, and other specialized health and safety requirements.
Promote a strong safety culture through leadership, mentoring, and continuous improvement.

Technical Reporting and Data Management

Prepare and review technical reports, groundwater monitoring reports, regulatory submittals, and field documentation.
Perform QA/QC reviews of environmental data, field records, and project deliverables.
Manage environmental databases and electronic reporting platforms, including EQuIS and GeoTracker.
Support data validation, interpretation, and presentation of technical findings to clients and regulatory agencies.

Team Development

Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior environmental professionals.
Coordinate multidisciplinary teams including environmental scientists, geologists, engineers, biologists, technicians, and subcontractors.
Support staff development through field training, technical mentoring, and knowledge sharing initiatives.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Biology, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources, or a related field and 4+ years environmental consulting or related professional experience (groundwater monitoring, environmental sampling, remediation field activities, and environmental compliance programs, leading project teams, coordinating complex environmental projects, experience preparing technical reports and regulatory deliverables, etc.) or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy.
Employment is contingent upon successfully completing a pre-employment background check and drug screen.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting California environmental remediation programs, including DTSC, RWQCB, and GeoTracker reporting requirements.
Experience at refinery, chemical, manufacturing, terminal, energy, or other industrial facilities, including CERCLA, RCRA, corrective action, and groundwater remediation programs.
Experience managing subcontractors, coordinating multidisciplinary project teams, and supporting emergency response and disaster recovery.
Experience with complex groundwater monitoring and reporting, environmental site investigations, remediation, compliance, and regulatory reporting.
Proficiency in EQuIS, GeoTracker, environmental database management, QA/QC, data validation, technical report preparation, SWPPP compliance, HASPs, JSAs, atmospheric and radiological monitoring.
Relevant training and certifications: current OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER, OSHA 8-Hour HAZWOPER Refresher, OSHA Site Supervisor Training, RCRA Hazardous Waste Management Training, Radiation Safety or Radiological Monitoring Training, Confined Space Entry Training, and First Aid/CPR Certification.

Additional Information

AECOM is unable to provide employment visa sponsorship now or in the future for this position.

Position may involve local and regional travel, field assignments, and periodic overnight travel.

Application materials cannot be accepted outside of the jobs portal. Applications cannot be edited on an applicant's behalf. For more information about the IRD and the applicant review process, view this link.

The IRD for this job is: 11-04-2026

About Uc Santa Cruz

UC Santa Cruz is a public university like no other in California, combining the experience of a small, liberal arts college with the depth and rigor of a major research university. It's known as an unconventional place where innovation and experimentation is part of the campus's DNA. That playful, bold spirit still thrives today, all on a campus renowned as among the most beautiful in the world.

Department Overview

Administratively located within the Finance, Operations, and Administration (FOA) division, our primary duties are to promote, facilitate, and provide expert consultation for EH&S programs in support of university operations. We are responsible for monitoring compliance with environmental, health and safety programs intended to minimize or prevent occupational injuries and illnesses in the workplace and to protect the quality of the surrounding environment. EH&S advises the campus community on responsibilities with respect to health, safety and environmental issues; recommends appropriate corrective actions; and helps implement new health and safety programs. EH&S also acts as liaison between UCSC and various external agencies and regulatory bodies. Our actions and decisions have the potential for high visibility and serious consequences to the campus and the community. EH&S programs include a broad and complex range of disciplines including areas such as laboratory and research safety, industrial hygiene, food safety, environmental management, diving and boating safety, radiation safety, hazardous materials control, ergonomics, biosafety, and fire safety.

More information can be found at: https://ehs.ucsc.edu/

Job Summary

The Hazardous Materials and Waste Manager serves as the technical expert for Hazardous Materials, Hazardous Waste, and Dangerous Goods Shipping. The position is responsible for three Waste Accumulation Areas (WAAs); coordinates chemical, medical, and universal waste collections; manages waste billing and manifest fees; and directly executes dangerous goods shipments. This position is highly active in auditing and reporting, it requires conducting weekly WAA inspections, annual non-lab hazmat inspections, and annual SPCC inspections; processing technical information to produce regulatory reports, such as California Environmental Reporting System (CERS) business plans, annual e-waste reports, and biennial waste reports; and delivers outreach and training to campus waste generators. The position oversees problems that are complex and may require creation of new methodologies by applying professional EH&S knowledge and expertise. They will also serve as the technical expert in the development and implementation of programs within these fields. Decision-making is based on established procedures, integration and interpretation of relevant laws, regulations and organizational policy; professional best practices; relevant science methodology, impact on other EH&S programs; and senior management approvals. Decisions may impact other EH&S programs, departments, segments of the organization and / or organization-wide.

APPOINTMENT INFORMATION

Budgeted Salary:
$100,100 - $107,674/annually. Salary commensurate with skills, qualifications and experience.

Under California law, the University of California, Santa Cruz is required to post a reasonable estimate of the compensation for this role. The salary shown above is the budgeted amount the University reasonably expects to pay and the salary extended should not exceed this posted amount.

Benefits Level Eligibility:
Full benefits

Schedule Information

Full-time, Fixed
Percentage of Time: 100%, 40 Hours per Week
Days of the Week: Mon-Fri
Shift Includes: Day

Employee Classification:
Career appointment

None

UC Santa Cruz Main Campus

Non-Represented

EHS SPEC 4 (000358)

Never or Rarely

Job Duties

40% - Hazardous Waste Program Management

Performs complex technical work in hazardous materials control, hazardous waste management, and shipping.

Chemical Waste Collection and Management: Weekly consolidation pick-ups, supporting offsite shipments, combined waste management, and chemo waste.
Medical Waste Management: Manage weekly waste pick-ups.
Universal Waste Management: Organize battery pick-ups and shipping.
Dangerous Goods Shipping: Execute dangerous goods shipments; complete shipper's declaration; review package compliance.
Waste Manifests Management: Organize and maintain official waste manifests.
Taxes and Fees: Ensure all waste manifest taxes and fees are allocated and paid appropriately.

Drafts reports and other documentation.

Waste Biennial Reporting: Gather data and write biennial waste reports.
Hazardous Materials Business Plan: Draft annual report, including its detailed inventories and maps.
E-waste Annual Report: Coordinate data collection and drafting the annual report on electronic waste.
Hazardous Materials Business Plan: Manage CERS (California Environmental Reporting System) compliance and program requirements.

20% - Outreach and Education

Performs outreach and communication to UCSC affiliate populations.

Waste and Hazmat Training: Design and provide training on related topics - Waste Generator and Manifests, WAA training, and Hazardous Materials Management.
Billing and Invoice Management: Handle billing, invoices, and consolidated billing for chemical waste, medical waste, and batteries.

Writes and updates manuals and procedures.

Maintain accurate and approachable online resources for hazardous materials and hazardous waste safety.

Provides expert counsel by evaluating, interpreting and applying laws, regulations, codes and standards.

Waste Evaluations: Provide evaluations of waste types and properties to determine proper handling and disposal protocols.

20% - Inspections and Compliance

Monitors compliance and prevents hazards, and may serve as organization liaison with regulatory agencies.

CUPA Inspection Liaison: Coordinate and manage agency inspection and corrective action follow-ups.
WAA (Waste Accumulation Area) Management: Oversee WAA operations, ensuring a clean, functional, and well-maintained facilities.

Inspects, investigates incidents and complaints, and recommends corrective action as needed.

Non-Lab Hazmat Inspections: Carry out inspections on non-research facilities that store hazardous chemicals, validate chemical inventories, monitor and support corrective actions.
SPCC Plan Annual Inspections: Perform annual inspections required for Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure plans.
